basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search (EO 13306 precedent). EO 10805 (signed 1959-02-18; 24 FR 1301; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10805.txt, read in full) designates the Central Intelligence Agency as excepted from certain provisions of the Government Employees Training Act and makes a conforming amendment to EO 10800. Identity: heading, title and date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory omitted the recitals and section 1 lead-in and ran subsection (d) together with section 2, so I replaced it with six clauses (inventory override). Own terms: no clause has an end date or ending condition. Later instruments: a search of the held order texts for the number 10805 finds only the order's own Federal Register copy and the 1989 codification snapshot; the dossier chain has no event and lists no missing line apart from the three standing current-law lines, which I read and rule out as bases because the basis of this claim is the held original text, not a current-law lead. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record no revocation or supersession of EO 10805; the U.S. Code leads (notes at 5 U.S.C. 4102 and 4108) are corroboration only and are not quoted because their text is not held. Limit stated plainly: the Act the order cites (Public Law 85-507) is not held, and I do not assert how its later recodification bears on the exceptions beyond the absence of any ending in the bounded searches; continuation of subsections (a) to (d) rests on the original text and those searches, and the U.S. Code edition runs through 2026-10-09.

By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 465 of the Revised ' 
Statutes (25 U.S.C. 9) and as President of the United States, the 
Secretary of the Interior is hereby designated and empowered to 
exercise, without the approval, ratification, or other action of the 
President or of any other officer of the United States, any and all 
authority conferred upon the United States by section 403(a) of the 
Act of April 11, 1968, 82 Stat. 79 (25 U.S.C. 1323(a)) : Provided, 
That acceptance of retrocession o f .  all or any measure of civil or 
criminal jurisdiction, or both, by the Secretary hereunder shall be 
effected by publication in the F e d e r a l R e g is t e r of a notice which 
shall specify the jurisdiction retroceded and the effective date of the 
retrocession : Provided further^ That acceptance of such retrocession 
of criminal jurisdiction shall be effected only after consultation by 
the Secretary with the Attorney General.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole operative paragraph designates and empowers the Secretary of the Interior, without further action of the President or any other officer, to exercise the authority conferred on the United States by section 403(a) of the Act of April 11, 1968 (25 U.S.C. 1323(a)), to accept retrocession of criminal and civil jurisdiction over Indian country. Two provisos govern how the Secretary acts: acceptance is effected by a Federal Register notice specifying the jurisdiction retroceded and the effective date, and acceptance of criminal jurisdiction follows consultation with the Attorney General. It is a standing designation with no end date or ending condition; each retrocession the Secretary accepts is a separate later fact that uses the designation without exhausting it. No held later order amends or revokes it, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search (EO 13306 precedent). EO 11435 (signed 1968-11-21; 33 FR 17339; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11435.txt, read in full) designates the Secretary of the Interior to accept, on behalf of the United States, retrocession by any State of criminal and civil jurisdiction over Indian country under section 403(a) of the Act of April 11, 1968. Identity: the heading, the title and the date of November 21, 1968 agree with the register row. The held text carries the order as one paragraph with two provisos; the dossier inventory instead listed six clauses cut from the next Federal Register page, which prints an unrelated milk indemnity regulation, so I corrected the inventory to one clause spanning the whole paragraph (inventory override, with the absolute span in the sheet). Own terms: no end date, sunset or ending condition. Later instruments: a search of the held order texts for the number 11435 finds only the order's own Federal Register copy and the 1989 codification snapshot; the dossier chain has no event and lists no unresolved missing line apart from the three standing current-law lines, which I read and rule out as bases because the basis of this claim is the held original text, not a current-law lead. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes and carry no coverage warning; they cover the U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09 (enactments of 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected, a stated limit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and the OFR catalog, and record no revocation, supersession or amendment of EO 11435. The Code note and CFR citations the leads point to are corroboration only and are not quoted because their text is not held. Limit: continuation rests on the original text and the absence of any ending in the bounded searches; the statute text (25 U.S.C. 1323) is not held, so I do not assert how the underlying authority stands beyond that.

basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search (EO 13306 precedent). EO 10967 (signed 1961-10-10, 'Administration of Palmyra Island', 26 FR 9667; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10967.txt, read in full) assigns civil administration of Palmyra Island to the Secretary of the Interior. The page also carries EO 10966, 10968 and 10969 (a tax-return inspection order, a traffic-safety amendment and an emergency board); I read only EO 10967's own text as the order. Identity: heading, title, signature date and filing line agree with the register row. The dossier's six clauses (sections 1 and 3 to 7, with the garbled section 2 inside the section 1 clause) are accepted as the inventory. Own terms: section 4 is the only duration term and is an event sunset (until Congress provides for civil administration of the island, or earlier presidential specification). I looked for either event in the three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog), read with their coverage notes, and in the held Federal Register originals by number and by name: no held later presidential instrument names EO 10967 or Palmyra Island administration (earlier Palmyra orders such as EO 8616 and EO 8682 are prior). The only machine leads are the U.S. Code note that prints the order (43 U.S.C. 1458 note) and an Office of the Federal Register note that section 4 contains a termination clause; neither records an event, and both are corroboration only and not quoted. Limit stated plainly: the statutes that would show whether Congress has provided for civil administration (the Hawaii Omnibus Act and the Act of June 15, 1950) are not held, so continuation rests on the original text and the absence of any ending event in the bounded searches (U.S. Code edition through 2026-10-09), not on a positive finding that the condition remains unmet.

Executive Order 10969
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE RE-  
TWEEN THE READING COMPANY  
AND CERTAIN OF ITS EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Reading Company, a carrier, and 
certain of its employees represented by 
the International Organization of Mas­
ters, Mates and Pilots, Local No. 14, a 
labor organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to" a degree such as 
to deprive a section of the eountry of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
UJS.C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate this dispute. No member 
of the board shall be pecuniarily or oth­
erwise interested in any organization of 
railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the dispute 
within thirty days from the date of this 
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
ehange, except by agreement, shall be 
made by The Reading Company or by 
its employees, in the condition out of 
which the dispute arose.
J ohn  F. K ennedy

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1(3) designates the Commission, except as to Presidential appointees, to exercise the President's authority under section 204 of the Act of June 30, 1932 and section 5(c) of the Civil Service Retirement Act to exempt a person from automatic separation when the public interest so requires. Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive Order 11228
PROVIDING FOR THE PERFORMANCE BY THE CIVIL SERVICE COMMIS­
SION OF CERTAIN FUNCTIONS VESTED IN OR SUBJECT TO THE AP­
PROVAL OF THE PRESIDENT
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 301 of Title 3 
of the United States Code, and as President of the United States, it is 
hereby ordered as follows—
S ec tio n 1 . The United States Civil Service Commission is hereby 
designated and empowered to exercise, without the approval, ratifica­
tion, or other action of the President, the following :
(1) The authority vested in the United States Civil Service Com­
mission by Section 605 of the Federal Employees Pay Act of 1945, 
59 Stat. 304 (5 U.S.C. 945), to issue, subject to the approval of the 
President, regulations necessary for the administration of certain 
provisions of that Act insofar as the Act affects officers and employees 
m or under the executive branch of the Government.
(2) The authority vested in the President by Section 203(f) of the 
Annual and Sick Leave Act of 1951, 65 Stat. 680 (5 U.S.C. 2062(f) ), 
to prescribe regulations governing the granting of leave of absence 
asdescribed in that Section.
(3) Except as to Presidential appointees, the authority vested in 
the President (A) by Section 204 of the Act of June 30,1932, 47 Stat. 
404, to exempt from automatic separation from the service under that 
Section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so re­
quires, and (B) by Section 5(c) of the Civil Service Retirement Act, 
70 Stat. 748 (5 U.S.C. 2255(c) ), to exempt from automatic separation 
from the service under Section 5 of that Act any employee when, in 
his judgment, the public interest so requires.
S e c. 2. The Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commis­
sion is hereby designated and empowered to exercise, without the ap­
proval, ratification, or other action of the President, the authority 
vested in the President by Section 304(e) of the Government Em­
ployees’  Incentive Awards Act, 68 S ta t 1113 (5 U.S.C. 2123(e)), to 
determine t,he activity primarily benefiting, or the various activities 
benefiting, from any suggestion, invention, superior accomplishment, 
or other personal effort of any civilian officer or employee of the 
Government which constitutes the basis of any Presidential award or 
honorary recognition made or granted under Section 304(b) of that 
Act (5 U.S.C. 2123(b) ).

(1) Part I I  of Executive Order No. 10530 of May 10,1954.

Wednesday, June 16, 1965 FEDERAL REGISTER 7741
Executive Order 11229
PARTICIPATION IN THE INTERNATIONAL COFFEE ORGANIZATION
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution of the 
United States of America, the International Coffee Agreement Act 
of 1965 (Public Law 89-23, approved May 22, 1965, hereinafter re­
ferred to as the A ct), the International Coffee Agreement, 1962, rati­
fied December 20, 1963, and proclaimed January 17, 1964 (TIAS 
5505, hereinafter referred to as the Agreement), and Section 301 of 
Title 3 of the United States Code, and as President of the United 
States, it is ordered as follows :
Section  1. /Secretary of State.  Subject to the provisions of this 
Order, the powers of the President involved in the participation of 
the United States of America in the Agreement, including so much 
of the functions conferred upon the President by the Act as is neither 
reserved nor delegated to other officers herein, are hereby delegated 
to the Secretary of State.
S e c. 2. Secretary of the Treasury.  The functions conferred upon 
the President by subsections (1) and (2) of Section 2 of the Act, 
together with the authority to issue and enforce such rules and regula­
tions as may be necessary to perform such functions, are hereby dele­
gated to the Secretary of the Treasury.
S e c. 3. Secretaries of State , the Treasury , Agriculture , Commerce, 
and Labor.  The functions conferred upon the President by subsec­
tion (3) of Section 2 of the Act, together with the authority to issue 
and enforce such rules and regulations as may be necessary to perform 
these functions, are hereby delegated to the Secretaries of State, the 
Treasury, Agriculture, Commerce, and Labor, severally.
S e c. 4. Functions reserved.  There are hereby reserved to the 
President the functions conferred upon him by Sections 5 and 8, and 
by the first sentence of Section 4 , of the Act.
S e c. 5. Coordination. The functions assigned by the provisions of 
this Order shall be performed under effective coordination. The meas­
ures of coordination hereunder shall include the following :
(1) In effecting and carrying out the participation of the United 
States of America in the Agreement, the Secretary of State shall con­
sult with the appropriate heads of Federal agencies, including the

By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 301 of Title 3 
of the United States Code, and as President of the United States, it is 
hereby ordered as follows—
S ec tio n 1 . The United States Civil Service Commission is hereby 
designated and empowered to exercise, without the approval, ratifica­
tion, or other action of the President, the following :
(1) The authority vested in the United States Civil Service Com­
mission by Section 605 of the Federal Employees Pay Act of 1945, 
59 Stat. 304 (5 U.S.C. 945), to issue, subject to the approval of the 
President, regulations necessary for the administration of certain 
provisions of that Act insofar as the Act affects officers and employees 
m or under the executive branch of the Government.
(2) The authority vested in the President by Section 203(f) of the 
Annual and Sick Leave Act of 1951, 65 Stat. 680 (5 U.S.C. 2062(f) ), 
to prescribe regulations governing the granting of leave of absence 
asdescribed in that Section.
(3) Except as to Presidential appointees, the authority vested in 
the President (A) by Section 204 of the Act of June 30,1932, 47 Stat. 
404, to exempt from automatic separation from the service under that 
Section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so re­
quires, and (B) by Section 5(c) of the Civil Service Retirement Act, 
70 Stat. 748 (5 U.S.C. 2255(c) ), to exempt from automatic separation 
from the service under Section 5 of that Act any employee when, in 
his judgment, the public interest so requires.
S e c. 2. The Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commis­
sion is hereby designated and empowered to exercise, without the ap­
proval, ratification, or other action of the President, the authority 
vested in the President by Section 304(e) of the Government Em­
ployees’  Incentive Awards Act, 68 S ta t 1113 (5 U.S.C. 2123(e)), to 
determine t,he activity primarily benefiting, or the various activities 
benefiting, from any suggestion, invention, superior accomplishment, 
or other personal effort of any civilian officer or employee of the 
Government which constitutes the basis of any Presidential award or 
honorary recognition made or granted under Section 304(b) of that 
Act (5 U.S.C. 2123(b) ).

(1) Part I I  of Executive Order No. 10530 of May 10,1954.

9,1961, as added paragraph (é) to Section 2 of Executive Order No. 
10530 of May 10,1954.

statute or to any provision of any statute shall be deemed to include 
references thereto as amended from time to time.

Wednesday, June 16, 1965 FEDERAL REGISTER 7741
Executive Order 11229
PARTICIPATION IN THE INTERNATIONAL COFFEE ORGANIZATION
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution of the 
United States of America, the International Coffee Agreement Act 
of 1965 (Public Law 89-23, approved May 22, 1965, hereinafter re­
ferred to as the A ct), the International Coffee Agreement, 1962, rati­
fied December 20, 1963, and proclaimed January 17, 1964 (TIAS 
5505, hereinafter referred to as the Agreement), and Section 301 of 
Title 3 of the United States Code, and as President of the United 
States, it is ordered as follows :
Section  1. /Secretary of State.  Subject to the provisions of this 
Order, the powers of the President involved in the participation of 
the United States of America in the Agreement, including so much 
of the functions conferred upon the President by the Act as is neither 
reserved nor delegated to other officers herein, are hereby delegated 
to the Secretary of State.
S e c. 2. Secretary of the Treasury.  The functions conferred upon 
the President by subsections (1) and (2) of Section 2 of the Act, 
together with the authority to issue and enforce such rules and regula­
tions as may be necessary to perform such functions, are hereby dele­
gated to the Secretary of the Treasury.
S e c. 3. Secretaries of State , the Treasury , Agriculture , Commerce, 
and Labor.  The functions conferred upon the President by subsec­
tion (3) of Section 2 of the Act, together with the authority to issue 
and enforce such rules and regulations as may be necessary to perform 
these functions, are hereby delegated to the Secretaries of State, the 
Treasury, Agriculture, Commerce, and Labor, severally.
S e c. 4. Functions reserved.  There are hereby reserved to the 
President the functions conferred upon him by Sections 5 and 8, and 
by the first sentence of Section 4 , of the Act.
S e c. 5. Coordination. The functions assigned by the provisions of 
this Order shall be performed under effective coordination. The meas­
ures of coordination hereunder shall include the following :
(1) In effecting and carrying out the participation of the United 
States of America in the Agreement, the Secretary of State shall con­
sult with the appropriate heads of Federal agencies, including the 
Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Agriculture, the Secretary 
of Commerce, and the Secretary of Labor.
(2) The delegates under Section 3 of this Order shall use the func­
tions delegated thereunder as they and the Secretary of State shall 
mutually agree. ^
S e c. 6. Redelegation.  Each Secretary mentioned in this Order is 
hereby authorized to redelegate within his Department the functions 
hereinabove assigned to him.
L yndon  B. J ohnson
T he  W h ite H ouse,
June 1965.

research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search (EO 13306 precedent). EO 11228 (signed 1965-06-14; 30 FR 7739; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11228.txt, read in full) designates the Civil Service Commission and its Chairman to exercise listed presidential functions without further presidential action. Identity: heading, title and date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory was incomplete (no section 2, no section 4(a), section 4(b) and section 5 run together, the section 3 list split from its lead-in), so I replaced it with nine clauses following the order's own structure (inventory override). Own terms: no clause has an end date or condition; section 5's 'until amended, modified, or revoked' concerns earlier actions kept in effect and 'sooner terminated by operation of law' is a general saving wording, not an end, and is read in the clause reason. Later instruments read in full where they name the order: EO 11257 (1965-11-13) inserts items (4) and (5) at the end of section 1 (Federal Employees Salary Act of 1965 severance-pay and exclusion authority); EO 12107 (signed 1978-12-28, effective 1979-01-01 under its section 2-404) lists EO 11228 in its section 2-101(b) and amends it by substituting the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission and the Director for the Chairman; both are amendments, attached as later events. EO 11619 (1971-09-22) only recites section 1 of EO 11228 and is not an amendment. The dossier's two 'target provision not located' lines (EO 11619, EO 12107) are resolved this way. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record no revocation or supersession of EO 11228; the Code notes and CFR provisions the leads point to are corroboration only and are not quoted. Limit stated plainly: the continuation of sections 1 and 2 rests on the original text, the two amendments and the absence of any ending in the bounded searches; the statutes cited in the order (several since recodified in title 5) are not held, so I do not assert their present text, and the U.S. Code edition runs through 2026-10-09.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1 (with the authority recital under section 501(a) of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973) provides that the Interagency Committee on Handicapped Employees is comprised of the named officials (or designees at executive level IV or higher): the Secretaries of Defense, Labor and Health, Education, and Welfare, the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission, the Administrators of Veterans Affairs and General Services, the Chairman of the Federal Communications Commission, and such other members as the President designates. It has no end term. EO 12106 (effective 1979-01-01 under its section 1-106) restated it in full (adding the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission Chairman as co-chairman and substituting the Director of the Office of Personnel Management); EO 12450 revised subsection (3) and added a Health and Human Services member; EO 12672 substituted subsection (10) and added subsections (11) and (12); and EO 12704 revised subsection (11). These amendments restate or change the membership list while the section continues, so under the strike-and-insert ruling they are later events, not ends; the substance of the membership has changed (note for the reviewer).

research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search (EO 13306 precedent). EO 11830 (signed 1975-01-09; 40 FR 2411; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11830.txt, read in full) enlarges the membership of the Interagency Committee on Handicapped Employees under section 501(a) of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973. Identity: heading, title and date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory was wrong (items (7) and (8) were merged with section 2 and the signature block; the authority recital was omitted), so I replaced it with two clauses, section 1 and section 2 (inventory override). Own terms: no end date or condition. Later instruments read in full where they name the order: EO 12106 section 1-105 deletes section 2 and restates section 1 (effective 1979-01-01 under its section 1-106); EO 12450 (1983-12-09) revises subsection (3), redesignates (9) as (10) and inserts a new (9); EO 12672 (1989-03-21) substitutes subsection (10) and adds (11) and (12); EO 12704 (1990-02-26) revises subsection (11) and adds a new section 2 naming the Committee. Section 2 is therefore ended by deletion on 1979-01-01, with EO 12704's new section 2 recorded as a later event; section 1 continues as restated and amended. The dossier chain also lists EO 11022 (1962) as an actor, which is a mislabel from the neighbouring page of EO 12106 (EO 11022 is the President's Council on Aging and does not mention EO 11830); I read it and attach nothing from it. The dossier's 'target provision not located: EO:12704' line is resolved. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record no revocation or supersession of EO 11830; the 29 U.S.C. 791 note and 32 CFR citations the leads point to are corroboration only and are not quoted. Limit: continuation of section 1 rests on the original text, the four amendments and the absence of any ending in the bounded searches (U.S. Code edition through 2026-10-09); a later order that I did not find because it does not cite EO 11830 by number could not be excluded by those searches.

source.quote:
Section 1
1- 1. Purpose and Scope.  The purpose of this Executive Order is to enable 
responsible officials of Federal agencies having ultimate responsibility for 
authorizing and approving actions encompassed by this Order to be informed 
of pertinent environmental considerations and to take such considerations 
into account, with other pertinent considerations of national policy, in making 
decisions regarding such actions. While based on independent authority, this 
Order furthers the purpose of the National Environmental Policy Act and the 
Marine Protection Research and Sanctuaries Act and the Deepwater Port Act 
consistent with the foreign policy and national security policy of the United 
States, and represents the United States government’s exclusive and complete 
determination of the procedural and other actions to be taken by Federal 
agencies to further the purpose of the National Environmental Policy Act, with 
respect to the environment outside the United States, its territories and 
possessions.

It has no end date or ending condition in the held text, and nothing held amends, revokes or supersedes it, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

encompassed hereby and not exempted herefrom having significant effects on 
the environment outside the geographical borders of the United States and its

consult with the Department of State and the Council on Environmental 
Quality concerning such procedures prior to placing them in effect.

2-3. Actions Included.  Agencies in their procedures under Section 2-1 shall 
establish procedures by which their officers having ultimate responsibility for 
authorizing and approving actions in one of the following categories encom­
passed by this Order, take into consideration in making decisions concerning 
such actions, a document described in Section 2-4(a):
(a) major Federal actions significantly affecting the environment of the global 
commons outside the jurisdiction of any nation (e.g., the oceans or Antarctica);
‘(b) major Federal actions significantly affecting the environment of a foreign 
nation not participating with the United States and not otherwise involved in 
the action;
(c) major Federal actions significantly affecting the environment of a foreign 
nation which provide to that nation:
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 44, NO. 6—TUESDAY, JANUARY 9, 1979

(1) a product, or physical project producing a principal product or an emission 
or effluent, which is prohibited or strictly regulated by Federal law in the 
United States because its toxic effects on the environment create a serious 
public health risk; or
(2) a physical project which in the United States is prohibited or strictly 
regulated by Federal law to protect the environment against radioactive 
substances.
(d) major Federal actions outside the United States, its territories and posses­
sions which significantly affect natural or ecological resources of global 
importance designated for protection under this subsection by the President, 
or, in the case of such a resource protected by international agreement binding 
on the United States, by the Secretary of State. Recommendations to the 
President under this subsection shall be accompanied by the views of the 
Council on Environmental Quality and the Secretary of State.

THE PRESIDENT 1957
Executive Order 12114 of January 4, 1979
Environmental Effects Abroad of Major Federal Actions
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the 
United States, and as President of the United States, in order to further 
environmental objectives consistent with the foreign policy and national 
security policy of the United States, it is ordered as follows:
Section 1
1- 1. Purpose and Scope.  The purpose of this Executive Order is to enable 
responsible officials of Federal agencies having ultimate responsibility for 
authorizing and approving actions encompassed by this Order to be informed 
of pertinent environmental considerations and to take such considerations 
into account, with other pertinent considerations of national policy, in making 
decisions regarding such actions. While based on independent authority, this 
Order furthers the purpose of the National Environmental Policy Act and the 
Marine Protection Research and Sanctuaries Act and the Deepwater Port Act 
consistent with the foreign policy and national security policy of the United 
States, and represents the United States government’s exclusive and complete 
determination of the procedural and other actions to be taken by Federal 
agencies to further the purpose of the National Environmental Policy Act, with 
respect to the environment outside the United States, its territories and 
possessions.
Sec. 2.
2- 1. Agency Procedures.  Every Federal agency taking major Federal actions 
encompassed hereby and not exempted herefrom having significant effects on 
the environment outside the geographical borders of the United States and its 
territories and possessions shall within eight months after the effective date of 
this Order have in effect procedures to implement this Order. Agencies shall 
consult with the Department of State and the Council on Environmental 
Quality concerning such procedures prior to placing them in effect.
2-2. Information Exchange.  To assist in effectuating the foregoing purpose, the 
Department of State and the Council on Environmental Quality in collabora­
tion with other interested Federal agencies and other nations shall conduct a 
program for exchange on a continuing basis of information concerning the 
environment. The objectives of this program shall be to provide information 
for use by decisionmakers, to heighten awareness of and interest in environ­
mental concerns and, as appropriate, to facilitate environmental cooperation 
with foreign nations.
2-3. Actions Included.  Agencies in their procedures under Section 2-1 shall 
establish procedures by which their officers having ultimate responsibility for 
authorizing and approving actions in one of the following categories encom­
passed by this Order, take into consideration in making decisions concerning 
such actions, a document described in Section 2-4(a):
(a) major Federal actions significantly affecting the environment of the global 
commons outside the jurisdiction of any nation (e.g., the oceans or Antarctica);
‘(b) major Federal actions significantly affecting the environment of a foreign 
nation not participating with the United States and not otherwise involved in 
the action;
(c) major Federal actions significantly affecting the environment of a foreign 
nation which provide to that nation:

(d) major Federal actions outside the United States, its territories and posses­

importance designated for protection under this subsection by the President,

provide for appropriate modifications in the contents, timing and availability 
of documents to other affected Federal agencies and affected nations, where

Title 3
The President
THE PRESIDENT 1957
Executive Order 12114 of January 4, 1979
Environmental Effects Abroad of Major Federal Actions
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the 
United States, and as President of the United States, in order to further 
environmental objectives consistent with the foreign policy and national 
security policy of the United States, it is ordered as follows:
Section 1
1- 1. Purpose and Scope.  The purpose of this Executive Order is to enable 
responsible officials of Federal agencies having ultimate responsibility for 
authorizing and approving actions encompassed by this Order to be informed 
of pertinent environmental considerations and to take such considerations 
into account, with other pertinent considerations of national policy, in making 
decisions regarding such actions. While based on independent authority, this 
Order furthers the purpose of the National Environmental Policy Act and the 
Marine Protection Research and Sanctuaries Act and the Deepwater Port Act 
consistent with the foreign policy and national security policy of the United 
States, and represents the United States government’s exclusive and complete 
determination of the procedural and other actions to be taken by Federal 
agencies to further the purpose of the National Environmental Policy Act, with 
respect to the environment outside the United States, its territories and 
possessions.
Sec. 2.
2- 1. Agency Procedures.  Every Federal agency taking major Federal actions 
encompassed hereby and not exempted herefrom having significant effects on 
the environment outside the geographical borders of the United States and its 
territories and possessions shall within eight months after the effective date of 
this Order have in effect procedures to implement this Order. Agencies shall 
consult with the Department of State and the Council on Environmental 
Quality concerning such procedures prior to placing them in effect.
2-2. Information Exchange.  To assist in effectuating the foregoing purpose, the 
Department of State and the Council on Environmental Quality in collabora­
tion with other interested Federal agencies and other nations shall conduct a 
program for exchange on a continuing basis of information concerning the 
environment. The objectives of this program shall be to provide information 
for use by decisionmakers, to heighten awareness of and interest in environ­
mental concerns and, as appropriate, to facilitate environmental cooperation 
with foreign nations.
2-3. Actions Included.  Agencies in their procedures under Section 2-1 shall 
establish procedures by which their officers having ultimate responsibility for 
authorizing and approving actions in one of the following categories encom­
passed by this Order, take into consideration in making decisions concerning 
such actions, a document described in Section 2-4(a):
(a) major Federal actions significantly affecting the environment of the global 
commons outside the jurisdiction of any nation (e.g., the oceans or Antarctica);
‘(b) major Federal actions significantly affecting the environment of a foreign 
nation not participating with the United States and not otherwise involved in 
the action;
(c) major Federal actions significantly affecting the environment of a foreign 
nation which provide to that nation:
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 44, NO. 6—TUESDAY, JANUARY 9, 1979

=== PDF page 16 of 200 ===
THE PRESIDENT
(1) a product, or physical project producing a principal product or an emission 
or effluent, which is prohibited or strictly regulated by Federal law in the 
United States because its toxic effects on the environment create a serious 
public health risk; or
(2) a physical project which in the United States is prohibited or strictly 
regulated by Federal law to protect the environment against radioactive 
substances.
(d) major Federal actions outside the United States, its territories and posses­
sions which significantly affect natural or ecological resources of global 
importance designated for protection under this subsection by the President, 
or, in the case of such a resource protected by international agreement binding 
on the United States, by the Secretary of State. Recommendations to the 
President under this subsection shall be accompanied by the views of the 
Council on Environmental Quality and the Secretary of State.

be used in connection with actions described in Section 2-3:
(i) environmental impact statements (including generic, program and specific 
statements);
(ii) bilateral or multilateral environmental studies, relevant or related to the 
proposed action, by the United States and one more foreign nations, or by an 
international body or organization in which the United States is a member or 
participant; or
(iii) concise reviews of the environmental issues involved, including environ­
mental assessments, summary environmental analyses or other appropriate 
documents.
(b) Agencies shall in their procedures provide for preparation of documents 
described in Section 2-4(a), with respect to actions described in Section 2-3, 
as follows:
(i) for effects described in Section 2-3(a), an environmental impact statement 
described in Section 2-4(a)(i);
(ii) for effects described in Section 2-3(b), a document described in Section 2- 
4(a)(ii) or (iii), as determined by the agency;
(iii) for effects described in Section 2-3(c), a document described in Section 2- 
4(a)(ii) or (iii), as determined by the agency;
(iv) for effects described in Section 2-3(d), a document described in Section 2- 
4(a)(i), (ii) or (iii), as determined by the agency.
Such procedures may provide that an agency need not prepare a new docu­
ment when a document described in Section 2-4(a) already exists.

judicial settlement of any case or to prevent any agency from providing in its

of the United States.

O w ners and congressional findings th at recognize:
1. the significant role which small business and wom en entrepreneurs can play 
in promoting full employment and balanced growth in our economy;

By the authority vested in me as President of the United States of America, in 
order to create a N ational W om en’s Business Enterprise Policy and to pre­
scribe arrangem ents for developing, coordinating and implementing a national 
program for wom en’s business enterprise, it is ordered as follows:

1-101. W ithin the constraints of statutory authority and as otherw ise perm it­
ted by law:
(a) Each departm ent and agency of the Executive Branch shall take appropri­
ate action to facilitate, preserve and strengthen wom en’s business enterprise 
and to ensure full participation by wom en in the free enterprise system.
(b) Each departm ent and agency shall take affirmative action in support of 
w om en’s business enterprise in appropriate program s and activities including 
but not limited to:
(1) m anagem ent, technical, financial and procurem ent assistance,
(2) business-related education, training, counseling and inform ation dissem i­
nation, and
(3) procurement.
(c) Each departm ent or agency em pow ered to extend Federal financial assist­
ance to any program or activity shall issue regulations requiring the recipient 
of such assistance to take appropriate affirmative action in support of 
w om en’s business enterprise and to prohibit actions or policies w hich dis­
crim inate against w om en’s business enterprise on the ground of sex. For 
purposes of this subsection, Federal financial assistance m eans assistance 
extended by w ay of grant, cooperative agreement, loan or contract other than 
a contract of insurance or guaranty. These regulations shall prescribe sanc­
tions for noncom pliance. Unless otherw ise specified by law, no agency sanc­
tions shall be applied until the agency or departm ent concerned has advised 
the appropriate person or persons of the failure to comply w ith its regulations 
and has determ ined that compliance cannot be secured by voluntary m eans.
1-102. For purposes of this Order, affirmative action m ay include, but is not 
limited to, creating or supporting new  program s responsive to the special 
needs of wom en’s business enterprise, establishing incentives to promote 
business or business-related opportunities for w om en’s business enterprise, 
collecting and dissem inating inform ation in support of w om en’s business 
enterprise, and insuring to wom en’s business enterprise knowledge of and

research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search (EO 13306 precedent). EO 12138 (signed 1979-05-18; 44 FR 29637; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12138.txt, read in full) creates a National Women's Business Enterprise Policy, directs departments and agencies to support women's business enterprise, and establishes the Interagency Committee on Women's Business Enterprise. Identity: heading, title and date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory was wrong (recital items taken as clauses, and one clause ran from section 1-101(c) to the end of the order), so I replaced it with the order's own sections, 27 clauses in all (inventory override). Own terms: no section has an end date or condition; the six-month period in section 1-307 and the annual report in section 1-501 are a deadline and a recurring duty, not ends. Later instruments: EO 12608 (signed 1987-09-09; 52 FR 34617), listed in its section 15, substitutes 'Department of Health and Human Services' for 'Department of Health, Education, and Welfare' wherever it occurs; this reaches only the department list in section 1-203, and I attach it to that clause. It states no effective date, so I use its signing date. The dossier's 'target provision not located: EO:12608' line is resolved this way. A search of the held order texts for the number 12138 finds no other instrument that amends, revokes or supersedes it. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record no revocation or supersession of EO 12138; the 15 U.S.C. 7101 note, 25 U.S.C. 5324 note and 13 CFR part 112 and 48 CFR citations the leads point to are corroboration only and are not quoted. Limit stated plainly: continuation rests on the original text, the single department-name amendment and the absence of any ending in the bounded searches; the U.S. Code edition runs through 2026-10-09, and later statutes touching women's business enterprise are not held, so I do not assert how they interact with the Committee.

Executive Order 12024 .  December 1,1977
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and statutes of the 
United States of America, including the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended 
(5 U.S.C. App. I), Section 301 of Title 3 of the United States Code, Section 202 of 
the Budget and Accounting Procedures Act of 1950 (31 U.S.C. 581c), and Section 7 
of Reorganization Plan No. 1  of 1977 (42 FR 56101 (October 21, 1977)), and as 
President of the United States of America^ in accord with the transfer of advisory 
committee functions from the Office of Management and Budget to the General 
Services Administration provided by Reorganization Plan No. 1  of 1977, it is hereby 
ordered as follows:
Section  1. The transfer, provided by Section 5F'of Reorganization Plan No. 1  of 
1977 (42 FR 56101), of certain functions under the Federal Advisory Committee Act, 
as amended (5 U.S.C. App. I), from the Office of Management and Budget and 
its Director to the Administrator of General Services is hereby effective.
Sec. 2. There is hereby delegated to the Administrator of General Services all the 
functions vested in the President by the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended, 
except that, the annual report to the Congress required by Section 6(c) of that Act shall 
be prepared by the Administrator for the President’s consideration and transmittal 
to the Congress.
Sec. 3. The Director of the Office of Management and Budget shall take all actions 
necessary or appropriate to effectuate the transfer of functions provided in this Order, 
including the transfer of funds, personnel and positions, assets, liabilities, contracts, 
property, records, and other items related to the functions transferred.
Sec. 4. Executive Order No. 11769 of February 21,1974 is hereby revoked.
Sec. 5. Any rules, regulations, orders, directives, circulars, or other actions taken 
pursuant to the functions transferred or reassigned as provided in this Order from the 
Office of Management and Budget to the Administrator of General Services, shall 
remain in effect as if issued by the Administrator until amended, modified, or revoked.
Sec. 6. This Order shall be effective November 20, 1977.

THE PRESIDENT 61445
[ 3195 - 0 1]
Relating to the Transfer of Certain Advisory Committee Functions
Executive Order 12024 .  December 1,1977
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and statutes of the 
United States of America, including the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended 
(5 U.S.C. App. I), Section 301 of Title 3 of the United States Code, Section 202 of 
the Budget and Accounting Procedures Act of 1950 (31 U.S.C. 581c), and Section 7 
of Reorganization Plan No. 1  of 1977 (42 FR 56101 (October 21, 1977)), and as 
President of the United States of America^ in accord with the transfer of advisory 
committee functions from the Office of Management and Budget to the General 
Services Administration provided by Reorganization Plan No. 1  of 1977, it is hereby 
ordered as follows:
Section  1. The transfer, provided by Section 5F'of Reorganization Plan No. 1  of 
1977 (42 FR 56101), of certain functions under the Federal Advisory Committee Act, 
as amended (5 U.S.C. App. I), from the Office of Management and Budget and 
its Director to the Administrator of General Services is hereby effective.
Sec. 2. There is hereby delegated to the Administrator of General Services all the 
functions vested in the President by the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended, 
except that, the annual report to the Congress required by Section 6(c) of that Act shall 
be prepared by the Administrator for the President’s consideration and transmittal 
to the Congress.
Sec. 3. The Director of the Office of Management and Budget shall take all actions 
necessary or appropriate to effectuate the transfer of functions provided in this Order, 
including the transfer of funds, personnel and positions, assets, liabilities, contracts, 
property, records, and other items related to the functions transferred.
Sec. 4. Executive Order No. 11769 of February 21,1974 is hereby revoked.
Sec. 5. Any rules, regulations, orders, directives, circulars, or other actions taken 
pursuant to the functions transferred or reassigned as provided in this Order from the 
Office of Management and Budget to the Administrator of General Services, shall 
remain in effect as if issued by the Administrator until amended, modified, or revoked.
Sec. 6. This Order shall be effective November 20, 1977.
T h e W hite  H o use,
December 1 , 1977.
[FR Doc.77-34952 Filed 12-2-77;10:5f am]

research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search (EO 13306 precedent). EO 12024 (signed 1977-12-01, effective 1977-11-20 under its section 6; 42 FR 61445; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12024.txt, read in full) gives effect to the transfer of Federal Advisory Committee Act functions from the Office of Management and Budget to the Administrator of General Services and delegates the President's FACA functions to the Administrator. Identity: heading, title and date agree with the register row. I confirmed the dossier's six section clauses as the complete inventory; the recital before section 1 is authority wording, not a command. Own terms: no section has an end date or condition (section 5's 'until amended, modified, or revoked' concerns kept-in-effect actions). Sections 1 and 4 are self-executing and are recorded as performed on the signing date, 1977-12-01 (section 6's earlier effective date, 1977-11-20, is retroactive and is not used as an end date); section 3 is an implementation command with no shown completion and is kept operative with that limit disclosed. Later instruments: the dossier chain labels EO 12078 (1978) and EO 12168 (1979-10-24) as 'terminate'; I read both. EO 12078 section 1-307 and EO 12053 section 4(c) only recite that FACA functions for those commissions are performed by the Administrator 'as provided by Executive Order No. 12024', so they neither end nor amend it. EO 12168 section 1-303 provides 'Notwithstanding Executive Order 12024' that the Director of the Office of Management and Budget performs the FACA functions for that Commission; I attach it as a limited exception to section 2 and not as an end. The dossier's 'cited by number, no change provision located: EO:12053' line is resolved this way. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record no revocation or supersession of EO 12024; the 5 U.S.C. 1002 note and 41 CFR citations the leads point to are corroboration only and are not quoted. Limit: continuation of sections 2, 3, 5 and 6 rests on the original text, the one attached exception and the absence of any ending in the bounded searches (U.S. Code edition through 2026-10-09).

No held order, statute text or search result ends EO 12024.","independent_command_check":"The delegation in section 2 does not depend on sections 1, 3 or 4 having continuing force: section 1's transfer and section 4's revocation were performed when the order issued on 1977-12-01, and the section 2 delegation is a separate standing command.","savings_check":"Section 5 preserves rules and actions taken under the transferred functions until amended, modified or revoked; it is operative with the order. Foreign Service A ct of 1980
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the 
United States of America, including the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (94 Stat.

research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search (EO 13306 precedent). EO 12292 (signed 1981-02-23, effective as of 1981-02-15 under its section 11; 46 FR 13967, titled 'Foreign Service Act of 1980'; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12292.txt, read in full) conforms existing Executive Orders to the Foreign Service Act of 1980: sections 1 to 9 each amend one named earlier order, section 10 revokes thirteen listed orders or parts, and section 11 sets the effective date. Identity: heading, title and date agree with the register row. The dossier's 40 clauses broke those sections into lettered paragraphs, so I replaced them with the order's 12 provisions (inventory override). Own terms: no section states an end date or ending condition. Sections 1 to 10 are self-executing: the amendments and revocations were performed when the order issued, so they are recorded as terminated on the signing date, 1981-02-23 (section 11 makes them effective as of February 15, 1981, a retroactive date I do not use as the end date); the amended wording continues in the other orders. The ordering formula and section 11 are standing text and stay operative. Later instruments: I searched the held Federal Register originals for EO 12292 by number (including spaced OCR forms) and found it named in no later held order. The dossier's chain events (EO 12365, 12399, 12423, 12458, 12560, 12608, 12639, 12680, 12695, 12738, 13030, 13091, 13118, 13346, 13361, 13656, 13724 and EO 9452) are leads about changes to the orders that EO 12292 itself amended or revoked, or neighbours on the same Federal Register pages (for example EO 12399 only continues advisory committees); none names or ends EO 12292, so none is attached as a later event. EO 9452 is revoked by EO 12292's section 10(a), not the other way round. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes and record no revocation or supersession of EO 12292; their references to 22 U.S.C. 3901 are corroboration only and are not quoted. Limit: the Foreign Service Act text is not held, and whether the amended orders still carry the 1980-Act wording today is a question about those orders, not this one (U.S. Code edition through 2026-10-09).

importance to national security of the Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program, and 
for the purpose of preserving the basic structure, policies, and practices 
developed for this Program in the past and assuring that the Program will 
continue to function with excellence, it is hereby ordered as follows:

carried out by two organizational units, one in the Department of Energy and 
the other in the Department of the Navy.

4979
Federal Register
Vol. 47, No. 2 3
Wednesday, February 3, 1982
Presidential Documents
Title 3— Executive Order 12344 of February 1, 1982
T h e President N a v a l N u c le a r  P rop ulsio n  Program
By the authority vested in me as President and as Commander in Chief of the 
Armed Eorces of the United States of America, with recognition of the crucial 
importance to national security of the Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program, and 
for the purpose of preserving the basic structure, policies, and practices 
developed for this Program in the past and assuring that the Program will 
continue to function with excellence, it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. The Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program is an integrated program 
carried out by two organizational units, one in the Department of Energy and 
the other in the Department of the Navy.
Sec. 2. Both organizational units shall be headed by the same individual so 
that the activities of each may continue in practice under common manage­
ment. This individual shall direct the Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program in 
both departments. The director shall be qualified by reason of technical 
background and experience in naval nuclear propulsion. The director may be 
either a civilian or an officer of the United States Navy, active or retired!
Sec. 3. The Secretary of the Navy (through the Secretary of Defense) and the 
Secretary of Energy shall obtain the approval of the President to appoint the 
director of the Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program for their respective Depart­
ments. The director shall be appointed to serve a term of eight years, except 
that the Secretary of Energy and the Secretary of the Navy may, with mutual 
concurrence, terminate or extend the term of^the respective appointments.
Sec. 4. An officer of the United States Navy appointed as director shall be 
nominated for the grade, of Admiral. A  civilian serving as director shall be 
compensated at a rate to be specified at the time of appointment.
Sec. 5. Within the Department of Energy, the Secretary of Energy shall assign 
to the director the responsibility of performing the functions of the Division of 
Naval Reactors transferred to the Department of Energy by Section 309(a) of 
the Department of Energy Organization Act (42 U .S.C. 7158), including as­
signed civilian power reactor programs, and any naval nuclear propulsion 
functions of the Department of Energy, including:
(a) direct supervision over the Bettis and Knolls Atomic Power Laboratories, 
the Expended Core Facility and naval reactor prototype plants;
(b) research, development, design, acquisition, specification, construction, 
inspection, installation, certification, testing, overhaul, refueling, operating 
practices and procedures, maintenance, supply support, and ultimate disposi­
tion, of naval nuclear propulsion plants, including components thereof, and 
any special maintenance and service facilities related thereto;
(c) the safety of reactors and associated navel nuclear propulsion'plants, and 
control of radiation and radioactivity associated with naval nuclear propul­
sion activities, including prescribing and enforcing standards and regulations 
for these areas as they affect the environment and the safety and health of 
workers, operators, and the general public;
(d) training, including training conducted at the naval prototype reactors of the 
Department of Energy, and assistance and concurrence in the selection, 
training, qualification, and assignment of personnel reporting to the director

and of personnel who supervise, operate, or m aintain naval nuclear propulsion 
plants; and
(e )^  adm inistration o f the N aval N uclear Propulsion Program, including over­
sight of program support in areas such as security, nuclear safeguards and 
transportation, public information, procurement, logistics/and fiscal m anage­
ment.
Sec. 6. W ithin the Departm ent o f Energy, the director shall report to the 
Secretary o f Energy, through the A ssistant Secretary assigned nuclear energy 
functions and shall serve as a Deputy A ssistant Secretary. The director shall 
have direct access to the Secretary o f Energy and other senior officials in the 
Department of Energy concerning naval nuclear propulsion matters, and to all 
other personnel who supervise, operate or m aintain naval nuclear propulsion 
plants and support facilities for the Departm ent of Energy.
Sec. 7. W ithin the Departm ent of the N avy, the Secretary o f the N avy shall 
assign to the director responsibility to supervise all technical aspects of the 
N av y ’s nuclear propulsion work, including:
(a) research, development, design, procurement, specification, construction, 
inspection, installation, certification; testing, overhaul, refueling, operating 
practices and procedures, m aintenance, supply support, and ultimate disposi­
tion, o f naval nuclear propulsion plants, including com ponents thereof, and 
any special m aintenance and service facilities related thereto; and
(b) training programs, including N uclear Power Schools o f the N avy, and 
assistance and concurrence in the selection, training, qualification, and assign­
ment o f personnel reporting to the director and o f Governm ent personnel who 
supervise, operate, or m aintain naval nuclear propulsion plants.
Sec. 8. W ithin the Departm ent o f the N avy, the Secretary o f the N avy shall 
assign to the director responsibility within the N avy for:
(a) the safety o f reactors and associated naval nuclear propulsion plants, and 
control o f radiation and radioactivity associated with naval nuclear propul­
sion activities, including prescribing and enforcing standards and regulations 
for these areas as they affect the environment and the safety and health of 
workers, operators, and the general public.
(b) adm inistration o f the N av al N uclear Propulsion Program, including over­
sight o f program support in areas such as security, nuclear safeguards and 
transportation, public information, procurement, logistics, and fiscal m anage­
ment.
Sec. 9. In addition to any other organizational assignm ents within the Depart­
ment of the N avy, the director shall report directly to the C h ie f of N aval 
Operations. The director shall have direct access to the Secretary o f the N avy 
and other senior officials in the Departm ent o f the N av y  concerning naval 
nuclear propulsion matters, and to all other Governm ent personnel who 
supervise, operate, or m aintain n aval nuclear propulsion plants and support 
facilities.
Sec.10. This Order is effective on February 1,1982.

basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search (EO 13306 precedent). EO 12344 (signed 1982-02-01, effective the same day under its section 10; 47 FR 4979; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12344.txt, read in full) sets out the structure, leadership and assignments of the Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program in the Department of Energy and the Department of the Navy. Identity: heading, title and date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory omitted the ordering formula and section 10, so I kept its section and subsection structure, extended section 1 to the ordering formula and added section 10 (inventory override, 19 clauses). Own terms: no section has an end date or ending condition. The eight-year term and the power to end or extend it in section 3 govern each director's appointment and are not an end of the clause. Later instruments: the dossier chain is empty and has no missing line beyond the three standing current-law lines, which I read and rule out as bases; a search of the held order texts for the number 12344 finds only the order's own Federal Register copy and the 1989 codification snapshot. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record no revocation, supersession or amendment of EO 12344 (the later-events catalog search has no hit for it); the 10 U.S.C. and 42 CFR leads are corroboration only and are not quoted because their text is not held. Limit stated plainly: continuation rests on the original text and the absence of any ending in the bounded searches (U.S. Code edition through 2026-10-09). The Department of Energy Organization Act and later statutes on the Program are not held, so I do not assert how statute bears on the order.

Title 3— 
The President 
Executive Order 13361 of November 16, 2004
Assignment of Functions Under the United States Leadership 
Against HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria Act of 2003
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including section 301 of title 3, 
United States Code, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. Executive Order 12163 of September 29, 1979, as amended, is 
further amended as follows: 
(a) in subsection 1–100(a), by striking the period at the end of paragraph 
(15), by inserting a semicolon at the end of paragraph (15), and by adding 
at the end thereof the following new paragraph: 
‘‘(16) the United States Leadership Against HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis, and 
Malaria Act of 2003 (Public Law 108–25)(the ‘‘HIV/AIDS Act’’), as amend-
ed, and amendments made by the HIV/AIDS Act, which the Secretary 
shall perform, in the case of section 304, after consultation with the 
Secretary of Health and Human Services.’’; 
(b) in section 1–701, by inserting, after subsection (g), the following new 
subsections: 
‘‘(h) Those functions conferred by section 1(f)(1) and section 
1(f)(2)(B)(ii)(VII) of the State Department Basic Authorities Act of 1956, 
as amended (22 U.S.C. 2651a). 
‘‘(i) Those functions conferred by section 202(d)(4)(C)(i) and (ii) of the 
HIV/AIDS Act, as amended.’’; 
(c) by adding at the end thereof the following new section: 
‘‘1–906. Implementation. In carrying out this order, officers of the United 
States shall ensure that all actions taken by them are consistent with 
the President’s constitutional authority to: (a) conduct the foreign affairs 
of the United States; (b) withhold information the disclosure of which 
could impair the foreign relations, the national security, the deliberative 
processes of the Executive, or the performance of the Executive’s constitu-
tional duties; (c) recommend for congressional consideration such measures 
as the President may judge necessary and expedient; and (d) supervise 
the unitary executive branch.’’. 
Sec. 2. Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise 
affect the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budget, administrative, or legislative proposals. 
Sec. 3. This order is intended only to improve the internal management 
of the executive branch and is not intended to, and does not, create any 
right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity

Presidential Documents
67633
Federal Register 
Vol. 69, No. 223
Friday, November 19, 2004
Title 3— 
The President 
Executive Order 13361 of November 16, 2004
Assignment of Functions Under the United States Leadership 
Against HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria Act of 2003
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including section 301 of title 3, 
United States Code, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. Executive Order 12163 of September 29, 1979, as amended, is 
further amended as follows: 
(a) in subsection 1–100(a), by striking the period at the end of paragraph 
(15), by inserting a semicolon at the end of paragraph (15), and by adding 
at the end thereof the following new paragraph: 
‘‘(16) the United States Leadership Against HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis, and 
Malaria Act of 2003 (Public Law 108–25)(the ‘‘HIV/AIDS Act’’), as amend-
ed, and amendments made by the HIV/AIDS Act, which the Secretary 
shall perform, in the case of section 304, after consultation with the 
Secretary of Health and Human Services.’’; 
(b) in section 1–701, by inserting, after subsection (g), the following new 
subsections: 
‘‘(h) Those functions conferred by section 1(f)(1) and section 
1(f)(2)(B)(ii)(VII) of the State Department Basic Authorities Act of 1956, 
as amended (22 U.S.C. 2651a). 
‘‘(i) Those functions conferred by section 202(d)(4)(C)(i) and (ii) of the 
HIV/AIDS Act, as amended.’’; 
(c) by adding at the end thereof the following new section: 
‘‘1–906. Implementation. In carrying out this order, officers of the United 
States shall ensure that all actions taken by them are consistent with 
the President’s constitutional authority to: (a) conduct the foreign affairs 
of the United States; (b) withhold information the disclosure of which 
could impair the foreign relations, the national security, the deliberative 
processes of the Executive, or the performance of the Executive’s constitu-
tional duties; (c) recommend for congressional consideration such measures 
as the President may judge necessary and expedient; and (d) supervise 
the unitary executive branch.’’. 
Sec. 2. Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise 
affect the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budget, administrative, or legislative proposals. 
Sec. 3. This order is intended only to improve the internal management 
of the executive branch and is not intended to, and does not, create any 
right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity

research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search (EO 13306 precedent). EO 13361 (signed 2004-11-16; 69 FR 67633; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13361.txt, read in full) amends EO 12163 to assign to the Secretary of State functions under the United States Leadership Against HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria Act of 2003. Identity: heading, title and date agree with the register row. I confirmed the dossier's seven clauses as the complete inventory (the section 1 lead-in, subsections (a) to (c) with the paragraph (16) text, and sections 2 and 3). Own terms: no clause has an end date or condition. Section 1's amendments of EO 12163 are self-executing and are recorded as performed on signing, 2004-11-16 (the order has no effective-date section); the inserted text is a surviving consequence in EO 12163, whose continuation this claim does not assess. Sections 2 and 3 are standing rules of construction and are the continuing clauses. Later instruments: the dossier chain lists EO 13656 (2014-01-17); I read it and it amends section 1-701(c) of EO 12163 by striking text after a semicolon, without naming EO 13361, so it is not a later event here. A search of the held order texts for the number 13361 finds no instrument other than the order itself. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record no revocation or supersession of EO 13361; the lead to a 22 U.S.C. 2381 note is corroboration only and is not quoted. Limit stated plainly: the order's present effect is mostly through the text inserted into EO 12163, which this claim does not trace; the continuing clauses recorded are the two construction clauses, and the U.S. Code edition runs through 2026-10-09.

The paragraph (16), subsections (h) and (i) and section 1-906 that section 1 inserted are now text of EO 12163 and survive as the consequence of the performed amendments; whether they remain in force depends on EO 12163 and is not assessed here.
